measures.subject: Conservation use property acreage limit
measures.ballotTitle: Shall the Constitution of Georgia, for the purpose of protecting family farmland, be amended so as to increase the maximum acreage to qualify for assessment and taxation as a bona fide conservation use property from 2,000 acres to 4,000 acres?
measures.summary: Raises the maximum acreage of a single owner's agricultural and timber land that can qualify for reduced conservation-use property tax assessment from 2,000 to 4,000 acres.

measures.subject: Nonpartisan election of probate judges
measures.ballotTitle: Shall the Constitution of Georgia be amended so as to require that all probate court judges be elected in nonpartisan elections?
measures.summary: Requires that all probate court judges in Georgia be elected in nonpartisan elections rather than with party labels.

measures.subject: Next Generation 9-1-1 Fund
measures.ballotTitle: Shall the Constitution of Georgia be amended so as to authorize the General Assembly to dedicate certain existing revenues, including revenues reallocated by law, to a nonlapsing fund to be used exclusively for the expansion, maintenance, and operation of emergency 9-1-1 systems in this state?
measures.summary: Allows the legislature to create a Georgia Next Generation 9-1-1 Fund and dedicate certain existing revenues to it, to be spent only on 9-1-1 systems.

measureEffectiveNote: Ga. Const. Art. X, Sec. I, Para. VI: unless the amendment or the resolution proposing it provides otherwise, a ratified amendment takes effect on January 1 following ratification. None of the three resolutions (HR 32, HR 251, HR 1243) sets another date, so all three would take effect January 1, 2027; Amendment 1's enabling statute is also reported (Capitol Beat) to take effect January 1, 2027.
notes: Candidate names and party labels are taken from official county sample ballots (SOS-generated ballot content). Georgia ballots print 'Republican' and 'Democrat' (some counties abbreviate 'Rep'/'Dem'). Candidates are listed in ballot order (Republican first).

Only Republicans and Democrats appear for statewide and congressional offices. Libertarians failed to regain ballot access in 2026; Chase Oliver (Governor), Allen Buckley (Senate), Thomas Blooming (PSC 5) and others are listed by Ballotpedia as withdrawn/disqualified.

Certified write-in candidates (left out per spec) exist for U.S. Senate, Governor, and House districts 10, 11, 13 and 14, per the SOS final write-in list published 2026-09-15 (reproduced in the White County sample ballot).
Two PSC seats (Districts 3 and 5) are elected statewide. Peter Hubbard (D, PSC 3) is the incumbent; PSC 5 is open (Tricia Pridemore did not run).

Printed ballot captions: Amendment 1 'Increases the maximum qualifying acreage for assessment and taxation as bona fide conservation use property.' (HR 32, Ga. L. 2025, p. 1081); Amendment 2 'Provides for the nonpartisan election of all probate court judges.' (HR 251, Ga. L. 2026, p. 1110); Amendment 3 'Authorizes creation of Georgia Next Generation 9-1-1 Fund for 9-1-1 systems expansion, maintenance, and operation.' (HR 1243, Ga. L. 2026, p. 1109). ballotTitle holds the question text only.
No statewide (statutory) referendum questions appear on the consolidated sample ballots reviewed; the SOS booklet covers 'Constitutional Amendments 1-3' only.
Georgia is entirely in the Eastern time zone; polls are open 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM. On Nov 3, 2026 that is EST (UTC-5), so 7:00 PM = 00:00 UTC Nov 4. Voters in line at 7:00 PM may still vote.

Name styling varies slightly by county: Fulton prints John "BONGO" Salvesen, DeKalb prints John "Bongo" Salvesen; Gwinnett prints Henry "Hank" Johnson Jr. without the comma DeKalb uses. Ballotpedia uses shorter/longer forms (e.g. James Kingston, Clayton Fuller, Sanford Bishop Jr., Pamela DeLancy) that differ from the ballots.
